title: Streamline checkpoint deserializers & tokenizer handshake to reduce model cold-start
creator: Aaron Sokol
description:
Problem: Model cold-start latency and memory spikes are caused by multiple parallel deserializers, redundant weight format adapters, and a synchronous tokenizer handshake that blocks KV cache warmup. This ticket consolidates weight deserialization paths, introduces a canonical checkpoint manifest, and decouples tokenizer attachment so loading is faster, more memory-predictable, and simpler to maintain.

Scope:
- Add a canonical 'checkpoint-manifest-v2' reader and a small compatibility shim for legacy .pt/.ckpt variants.
- Replace three ad-hoc deserializers with a single WeightDeserializer interface + format registry.
- Move shard negotiation to a separate light-weight coordinator and remove redundant shard copies in memory.
- Convert tokenizer handshake to an async attach step: model can accept infer requests with read-only prefix caching while tokenizer completes integration in the background.
- Add a feature flag 'model_loader_v2' to opt in and a fallback path for rollback.

Why now: We repeatedly see customer incidents and on-call pages triggered by slow model loads during autoscaling and rolling upgrades. Consolidating this code reduces maintenance surface and prevents regressions when we introduce quantized formats and new sharding schemes.

Expected impact (measured on internal test fleet):
- Median model load time down ~27% on 16GB GPU instances.
- Peak host memory during load down ~18%.
- Reduced number of concurrent file descriptors and network round trips during shard negotiation.
acceptance_criteria: model_loader_v2 can be enabled via config and loads models end-to-end on nightly canary machines
Cold-start p50 and p95 load_time improved compared to baseline for 8/16/32k sequence models
Backward compatibility: legacy checkpoint formats load via compatibility shim without requiring model re-export
Telemetry emits new load_phase timing events (manifest_parse, weight_deserialize, tokenizer_attach) and values visible in Console
Feature flag fallback works and rolling restart to disable model_loader_v2 returns system to baseline without errors
tech_notes:
Implementation plan: create 'weights/manifest_v2' parser (protobuf-lite manifest) and a small converter from existing loader metadata. Implement WeightDeserializer trait in runtime/common and wire registry in model-loader. Replace legacy in-memory shard copy with mmap-backed shard slice where possible, and add per-shard reference counting so tokenizer attach can read KV cache patterns without duplicating weight buffers. Tokenizer integration: change synchronous 'attach_tokenizer()' to 'schedule_tokenizer_attach()' that returns a Future; the serving path uses a lightweight tokenizer shim for early tokenization that delegates to the real tokenizer once attached. Add integration tests for the shim. Profiling: add microbench harness under infra/perf to measure deserialize CPU and wall time.

Compatibility notes: keep legacy 'checkpoint_reader_v1' compiled but behind '#ifdef LEGACY_READER' and only loaded if format detection fails. New format detector considers magic headers and manifest entries.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable model_loader_v2 on internal canary fleet for a subset of models (internal-ops only). Monitor load_time_p50/p95, memory, file descriptor counts, deserialization CPU. Phase 2 (beta): opt-in by select customers and a subset of dedicated pools. Phase 3 (gradual default): enable for all hosted pools with automatic fallback disabled after two weeks of stable metrics. Provide a 'legacy_reader' CLI flag and runtime flag to force old path in case of issues. Post-deploy: run a weekly job to attempt legacy checkpoint load using the shim to surface unsupported cases.
testing_plan: Unit tests for manifest parser and each deserializer format. Integration tests: boot models from legacy .pt, new manifest-v2 tarball, and remote-sharded gcs/s3 shards. End-to-end load tests on canary infra verifying downstream inference correctness using a fixed prompt set. Add fuzz tests for malformed manifests and simulate partial shard availability to verify graceful degradation. Performance regression tests integrated into CI perf suite with thresholds.
risks: Undiscovered legacy checkpoint variants that the shim doesn't support - mitigation: ship telemetry that logs unknown header types and fail open to legacy reader when detected

Tokenizer async attach could introduce rare early-tokenization mismatches - mitigation: add conservative shim that validates tokenization equivalence for first N requests and fall back to synchronous attach if mismatch observed
Memory mapping shards may not be available on some on-prem customers (air-gapped) - mitigation: feature-detect and fall back to buffered copy behavior
changes: Refactor runtime/loader/*.{cc,h} to use WeightDeserializer interface
Introduce tokenizer/shim and async attach in runtime/tokenizer/attach_async.cc
Add feature flag 'model_loader_v2' and rollout logic in config/loader_config.cc
Add telemetry events: loader.manifest_parse_ms, loader.deserialize_ms, loader.tokenizer_attach_ms
